description.en: Faith47's Solar Logos was made for Tbilisi Mural Fest 2021 and stands at 4 Atoneli Street. The title points to a solar, emblematic image, one of the festival's early large walls in the old town.

title.en: Georgian Artists - Street Art Sakartvelo Festival

description.en: Painted for the Street Art Sakartvelo festival, this Masholand (Masho Marg) mural is an homage to two Georgian cultural figures: singer-songwriter Inola Gurgulia and writer Guram Dochanashvili. The artist uses the wall to explore her own feelings for their work and the worlds they created. A cultural-tribute stop along Shalva Nutsubidze Street.

Painted during the 2017 Fabrikaffitti festival, this is another Masholand (Masho Marg) mural in the Fabrika yard. Two dragon fruits climb over the courtyard gate, one above each of its separate doors, so the piece reads as a playful pair. Look up at the gate to catch both halves together.

Masholand's (Masho Marg) very first mural, created for the 2016 Fabrikaffitti festival on the same Fabrika courtyard building as her later Dragon Fruit's Children. Painted in acrylics, which the artist says gave the characters a lively, stand-out quality against the wall. A small but important corner for followers of Tbilisi street art.

A colourful mural marking two firsts: Masholand's (Masho Marg) first collaboration with Niko Movement in Tbilisi and her first large exterior wall in the city. The work bridges her practice and the street, giving the neighbourhood a bright landmark. Stand back on Vasil Petriashvili Street to take in the full scale.

title.en: Who Is The Most Inspiring Woman For You?

description.en: Painted in Vaso Godziashvili's Park, this mural poses a direct question to passers-by. Masholand (Masho Marg) frames each person as an inner universe whose windows open through self-confidence and self-acceptance, a process she ties to women's experience. Expect a reflective, conversation-starting piece rather than a purely decorative one.

Painted for LG Georgia with the FCB marketing team to launch the brand's new direction in the city. Masholand (Masho Marg) covered over 90 square metres in roughly four days, making it one of her larger local walls. Its scale and finish suit the corporate brief, and it is easy to spot from Marshal Archil Gelovani Avenue.

Created for the Niko Movement festival, this Masho Marg (formerly Masholand) mural began with a simple aim: to bring colour and life to a grey street dominated by auto-parts shops and mechanical workshops. Seasonal imagery turns an overlooked wall into a vivid autumn scene, visibly changing the mood of the block.

title.en: A Small Wall for the Fleabag61

description.en: A small mural made for the Fleabag61 vintage store in an old Tbilisi neighbourhood. The client suggested the idea, while Masholand (Masho Marg) drew the sketch and executed it herself, so the piece is a compact, personal commission. Watch for it beside the shopfront on Giorgi Chubinashvili Street.

Part of Tina Chertova's 'Blue Tablecloth' project for Tbilisi Mural Fest, an ornamental series that also appeared in Tbilisi and Kutaisi. The artist describes it as 'ornamental storytelling of history', built on traditional Georgian ornaments and folk patterns. In Gori the blue field and pale ornament work over a facade on Stalin Avenue.

Tina Chertova turns Georgian folk ornament into a modern 'Blue Tablecloth' spread across the wall. She mixed motifs from old pattern books, then hid the story of a woman entrepreneur in the design, a writer, a doctor, an agronomist and a winemaker. Painted for Tbilisi Mural Fest on Bakhtrioni Street.

Sasha Korban painted this wall for Tbilisi Mural Fest 2023 on Lado Asatiani Street in the old town. The title Last Bell evokes the end-of-school-year ritual that closes a childhood chapter across the region, a quiet and nostalgic subject well suited to a residential street.

Case Maclaim's mural for Tbilisi Mural Fest 2024 stands on Ilia Chavchavadze Avenue. The title Mariam gives the large festival facade a personal, Georgian name, anchoring the work in the everyday life of one of the city's main arteries.

Painted for Tbilisi Mural Fest 2025 near Avlabari metro, this large wall by Afzan Pirzade and Besik Maziashvili is titled Mother and Child (Most Sacred Connection). The bond between parent and child is rendered at facade scale, greeting commuters in one of the city's busiest districts.

Italian artist Edoardo Ettorre made this work for Tbilisi Mural Fest 2025 as part of a series about looking beyond. Two little girls try to lift a plant to the top of the building so it can reach the light it needs, a simple scene about our responsibility to nature.

Dante painted Tsdo as the second collaboration between the Niko street-art movement and the Georgian National Ballet Sukhishvilebi. The mural freezes a move from the dance Tsdo, translating Georgian stage choreography into a static image on Davit Aghmashenebeli Avenue.

Batumi's edition of Tbilisi Mural Fest 2024 brought JDL to Pushkin Street for Rebirth. The wall adds a large contemporary piece to the seaside city's growing festival collection, pairing a European festival artist with a Batumi facade.

Tina Chertova painted Freedom for Women for the Niko Movement street-art festival in Batumi. Set on the city's E70 artery, the mural links her feminist, human-rights-driven practice to a public wall in Georgia's busiest resort city.

Gamez created Kupata the Friendly Dog to immortalise a beloved local character, the friendliest dog in Batumi, during the second Niko festival. The mural turns a Memed Abashidze Avenue wall into a citywide in-joke that residents recognise immediately.

Rosto's Elephant in the Air was made for the second Niko festival in Poti and sits on the city bus station. The placement gives travellers arriving or leaving the port city a playful, surreal image to pass, a signature of the festival's approach.

For the Gori edition of Tbilisi Mural Fest 2025, TMF Studio and Afzan Pirzade painted a Georgian Dance series on Dimitri Amilakhvari Street. The work brings the festival's folk-dance imagery into central Gori, a city better known for its Soviet-era history.

Vesod painted Am1ran1 in Kutaisi as his take on the Georgian mythological hero Amirani, a Prometheus-like figure chained for stealing fire. The piece joins the city's cluster of myth-themed festival murals, including its cycle devoted to Medea and Jason.

Ksyu Brice calls this his first personal mural in Georgia, composed like a postage stamp. A pomegranate, his most vivid first impression of the country and a symbol of its juiciness of life, sits beside a crane seen wild in Guria, standing for freedom. Painted on Lado Asatiani Street, Kutaisi.

JDL's Hold Me Tight was made for Tbilisi Mural Fest 2021 and stretches up to sixty metres, one of the largest walls of its edition. The artist asks viewers to appreciate the beauty of weakness, a gentle counterpoint to the mural's enormous scale on Tornike Eristavi Street.

Mohamed L'Ghacham painted Ilias's Room for Tbilisi Mural Fest 2022 on a wall in the Varketili district. The title suggests a private, domestic interior scaled onto a public facade, a quiet image dropped into a large housing estate.

Chilean artist Javier Barriga made Close to Me for Tbilisi Mural Fest 2024, drawing on the poem Apegado a mi by Nobel laureate Gabriela Mistral. The tender, maternal text shapes a large facade piece about closeness and protection in the city.

Sasha Korban's Ukrainian Girl stands on Ilia Chavchavadze Avenue. The portrait brings a figure from the war in Ukraine onto a Tbilisi facade, a reminder of the conflict just across Georgia's northern border.

title.en: but in the end, there will just be silence again

description.en: Christian Boehmer painted this long-titled wall on Akaki Tsereteli Avenue in 2022. The phrase 'but in the end, there will just be silence again' gives the mural a reflective, elegiac tone within a busy transport corridor of the city.

George Gamez's Phiso carries the motto 'sporty, arty, healthy, creative', pointing to a sports and community setting. The mural pairs athletic energy with street-art colour on a Tbilisi wall marked by the plus code QQ6H+2QW.

Tamoonz painted The Wave on the wall of Batumi's art school. The composition captures the atmosphere of the seaside city: hot summer suns and fire flames turning into time portals, a magical world of art fitting for the building where students make their work.

Musya painted Vaccinated for the Niko Movement festival in Batumi in 2021, when the pandemic dominated daily life. The title references the vaccine rollout of that year, making the mural a time capsule of a strange, anxious period on Zurab Gorgiladze Street.

David Samkharadze painted Medea for the second Niko festival in Poti, on Vakhtang Gorgasali Street. Medea, the sorceress of Greek myth long linked to Georgia's Colchis, recurs across the country's murals, and here she anchors a wall in the port city.

Gviriloba takes its name from a Kutaisi charity celebration first held in 1911, started by philanthropist Alexandra 'Sasha' Chikovani. In the mural by Oto Mikadze and Irine Kimberg, two intertwined daisies form a DNA helix, suggesting that standing together is written into the city's code.

Tina Chertova's Georgian Ornament brings her textile-inspired approach to Kutaisi's David Agmashenebeli Avenue. The wall continues the Blue Tablecloth family of works she made across Tbilisi, Kutaisi and Gori for Mural Fest.

Gera1's Mokhevian was painted for Tbilisi Mural Fest 2023. The title points to the Mokhevian highland people of Georgia, giving the wall a strong sense of place and local identity within the festival's spread across the city.

Argentine artist Milu Correch painted Medea on Simon Chikovani Street in 2023, joining the many Georgian murals devoted to the mythic Colchian woman. The large facade gives the classical character a monumental, contemporary setting.

Sasha Korban dedicated this Tbilisi Mural Fest 2023 wall to Maro Makashvili, the young Georgian nurse who died in the 1921 Soviet invasion and became a national heroine. The subject ties the festival to a formative, painful moment in modern Georgian history.

Goga Katsarava's Please Come Down! revives a childhood phrase everyone once shouted while playing. During painting, neighbours came out to cheer the idea as their own, and the artist credits locals for helping bring the nostalgic wall on Rafael Agladze Street to life.

Sepe's Portrait is inspired by ordinary, everyday situations and people's lives, which the artist uses as a starting point to explore composition, colour and form. Painted in Batumi, the work begins from daily life and drifts toward abstraction, letting the image live its own free, modified life.

Kera1 painted Center as a basketball-court mural for the Niko Movement festival in Batumi. Sited at Shota Rustaveli State University, it turns a court into a giant artwork, so students literally play on the mural.

Masholand (Masho Marg) painted Calm Flamingo for the third Niko festival in Batumi. The mural adds a calm, bright animal figure to Zurab Gorgiladze Street, part of the artist's long run of festival walls across Georgia.

Goga Katsarava made Cow-mosquito for the third Niko festival in Poti. The playful hybrid creature on Gegidze Street fits the artist's taste for humour and local storytelling, one of several festival walls dotted around the port city.

Greek artist INO painted Bleeding Heart in Kutaisi's Nikea district, where Tbilisi Mural Fest has gathered a cluster of myth-themed walls. The piece shows Jason and forms a visual dialogue with a nearby Medea mural, retelling the lovers' tragic story as a pair.

Sasha Korban's Old Woman is painted on Varlamishvili Street in Kutaisi. A close, unsentimental portrait by one of the festival's most recognisable artists, it adds a human, everyday presence to the city's growing open-air collection.

Pablo named Tita after a grape variety grown in Vazisubani, Tbilisi's vineyard district. Painted for Tbilisi Mural Fest 2023, the wall celebrates the area's long winemaking tradition, tying a contemporary mural to the landscape and craft of the neighbourhood.

Afzan Pirzade and Besik Maziashvili created Abkhazia is Georgia for Tbilisi Mural Fest 2025 on the Tskneti Highway. The mural carries an explicit political and territorial message at the entrance to the capital, one of the festival's most pointedly civic works.

Skv.art's Simple Wishes is part of Tbilisi Mural Fest 2025, on Tina Iosebidze Street. The title suggests small, everyday hopes, giving the wall an understated, personal note within the festival's large-scale production.

David Samkharadze's portrait of Vazha-Pshavela honours the famous Georgian writer and poet on the avenue that bears his name. The mural was dedicated to the writer's birthday, making it a monument as much as a street portrait.

Berlin-based JuMu Monster, of Peruvian and Chilean roots, painted Phoenix Carpet on Vazha Pshavela Avenue. The phoenix stands for a new beginning, arranged as a traditional carpet with floral elements, vases and a sun, motifs the artist gathers from travels.

Krashkid filled the wall of a Batumi art school with small scenes of characters chilling, reading and carrying materials, using the staircase as part of the composition. The building, on Niko Pirosmani Street, survives as a piece of old Batumi amid the city's construction boom.

Masholand's Medea's Heritage was made in Poti in collaboration with the Bank of Georgia and the Niko Movement. The piece links the port city to the Colchian Medea myth and continues the artist's run of large festival walls across the country.

Musya painted Beauty Drowning in Swamp for the third Niko festival in Poti. The title and image pair the beautiful with the murky, a contrast that suits the wetland landscape around this Black Sea port on Khobi Street.

Thiago Mazza's Flowers covers a Kutaisi wall with the artist's signature dense botanical painting, massing leaves and blossoms across the facade. The work is part of the festival's ongoing programme of murals across the city.

Pablo dedicated this Kutaisi mural to Zurab Sakandelidze, one of the country's most loved basketball players. The artist said he wanted to make something familiar for the city and its people, painting a move from the darker past into the colourful future.

A titled piece on Dimitri Uznadze Street in central Tbilisi, recorded by Street Art Cities without an attributed artist. Be Chill joins the run of independent street works on facades away from the festival clusters, a small surprise for passers-by.

Chill's mural combines the Georgian alphabet with graffiti, treating letters as energy and form. The artist notes the script is one of the oldest ways of mapping reality, while graffiti is the most direct modern art because it needs no gallery. Purple letters spell out a Georgian alphabet across the wall.

Matthias painted a typical Georgian street dog against a traditional patterned background. In Georgia street dogs are treated as part of the community, cared for and free, and the artist links them to solidarity and resilience, recalling how Niko Pirosmani portrayed them as soulful beings.

A Belarusian-Georgian collaboration on strong women in both countries' literature. Tina Chertova painted Georgian writer and feminist Ekaterine Gabashvili, who founded a school for women in need; Alena Davidovich added Belarusian poet Larissa Ganiush with a line of her verse.

Christian Böhmer painted Imagine Peace as a response to the 23 February invasion of Ukraine. Made for the Niko movement, the wall on Akaki Tsereteli Avenue turns a political statement into a large public image of peace.

Kelber's In Love was made for the Niko Movement festival in 2021. Sited on Bakhtrioni Street, the mural is one of two Kelber works on the same building, the other being Air, part of the festival's spread through the neighbourhood.

Lion Fleischmann painted 4GB crowd for the 4GB festival during the second Niko festival in 2019. The mural stands on a rural road outside Tbilisi, one of the open-air works that brought street art beyond the city centre.

Tina Chertova painted Queen Tamara for the third Niko festival in Tbilisi. The mural depicts the celebrated medieval Georgian monarch on Ivane Javakhishvili Street, tying contemporary street art to one of the country's most enduring historical figures.

Lamb's Supra celebrates the Georgian feast, the table that anchors hospitality and togetherness. Painted in 2016 on Davit Aghmashenebeli Avenue, it is an early example of the mural wave that turned Tbilisi's walls into a public gallery.

Musya's Swimming with Plastic shows a girl swimming among marine life and plastic bags. Made for the Niko movement, the mural on Dimitri Uznadze Street uses a gentle image to point at the pollution filling the seas.

A Street Art Cities entry titled Tied, painted on Larsi Turne in Tbilisi and recorded without an artist. The small wall belongs to the city's scattered independent street art, away from the larger festival commissions.

Musya reflects on our relationship with nature as a kind of game, using Tetris as the metaphor: city blocks and pixels crowd out greenery. The mural on Korneli Kekelidze Street asks viewers to grow cities without losing the environment we depend on.

Vadik Fin created an urban garden for the pheasant, an endangered bird and a symbol of Tbilisi. The artist links the bird to familial happiness and loyalty to the homeland, filling the wall near Lado Asatiani Street with bright colour and layered, slowly revealing forms.

title.en: The day will come when the war is over

description.en: Sasha Korban's The Day Will Come When the War Is Over carries a line about those who will see their loved ones again and those who will not. Painted for the Niko movement in 2022, it is one of several Tbilisi murals responding to the war in Ukraine.

nascaone painted Coyote for the Niko Movement festival in 2021 on Bakhtrioni Street. The mural belongs to the artist's animal imagery and to the festival's lively run of walls through central Tbilisi.

David Samkharadze painted Nature Looking Back for the second Niko festival in 2019. Set on Omar Khizanishvili Street in the north of the city, the mural continues the artist's portrait and nature subjects within the festival programme.
Tamoonz made A Girl with Crystal for the third Niko festival in Tbilisi. On Giorgi Chubinashvili Street, the mural adds a striking figure to a neighbourhood that now carries several festival walls.

Lamb's Gangsta Feast sits in an underground passage on Ilia Chavchavadze Avenue. A companion to the artist's Supra, it recasts the Georgian feast in a streetwise idiom, one of the early murals of the city's 2016 wave.

Luka Japaridze's Rebelion is described simply as a colourful revolution. Painted for the Niko movement in 2018 on Giorgi Dzotsenidze Street, the mural is one of the artist's early contributions to Tbilisi's festival scene.

Chil One's The Black Prince pays tribute to Kutaisi's pioneering 1990s hip-hop scene. The wall stands in the same block where the Black Prince, of the group Dzebnilebi and Jeronimo, lived, and the artist quotes one of their earliest songs.

INO painted Overthinker for the mural festival at Kutaisi International University. The work belongs to a group of campus murals that gathered international names at the same site near Chognari, turning the university into an open-air gallery.

INO's Blue Angel was made for the mural festival at Kutaisi International University. Together with Overthinker and other campus walls, it forms part of the festival's cluster of works at the university site near Chognari.

A Street Art Cities entry titled Portrait of a Girl, painted on Revaz Tabukashvili Street in Tbilisi with no attributed artist. It joins the many unattributed street works that fill the city's central lanes.

Dante and Pablo painted a portrait of footballer Shota Arveladze on Platon Ioseliani Street. The quote on the wall recalls his childhood disbelief that someone would paint a huge mural of him in an Ajax shirt in the city where he grew up.
Kade and Beka painted Girl on a Scooter on Akaki Tsereteli Avenue, marked by the plus code PQMJ+QV6. The mural adds a light, moving figure to one of the city's main arterial roads.

Part of Wow Wall Studio's My Home project supporting people forced to flee, this mural depicts a Belarusian girl with her child who moved to Tbilisi. She wears a dress patterned like a Belarusian dyvan, set against Georgian folk patterns, painted in gratitude for Georgia's hospitality.

Telmo Miel's Carry On portrays a young adult carrying their culture toward a bright future, on Abastumani Street in Tbilisi. The artist describes it as a life journey in which heritage travels alongside ambition across the wall.

DANTE dedicated this mural to the Sukhishvili Georgian National Ballet, made for the Niko street art festival in 2022. Khorumi, an ancient war dance, is rendered in the artist's graphic style on Petre Kavtaradze Street.

Pablo's Champions is a basketball-court mural made for the Niko Movement festival in 2021. Painting the court itself turns a sports surface into the artwork, so players step onto the mural every game.

Tina Chertova made Supporting Girls for the second Niko festival in Tbilisi in 2019. On Ilia Chavchavadze Avenue, the mural reflects her long focus on girls and women, a thread running through her festival work.

Levan Abramishvili painted Urban Garden for the third Niko festival in Tbilisi. The wall addresses the theme of greenery in the city, among the collection of festival murals in the eastern Varketili district.

Shota Saganeidze painted the face of Barbare Jorjadze, a nineteenth-century writer, women's-rights activist and leading Georgian feminist. The portrait uses alphabetic forms and patterns, giving a historical figure a distinctly street-art treatment.

Masholand's Escape from Masholand, described as an escape into masholand, was made for the Niko movement in 2018 on Vasil Petriashvili Street. The playful title and image mark the artist's growing presence on Tbilisi's walls.
Masholand (Masho Marg) painted Fireflies for the third Niko festival in Kutaisi. On Tamar the Queen Street, the mural adds a warm, glowing image to the city's growing collection of festival walls.

Feo Flip's Hunter occupies a wall on Egnate Ninoshvili Street in Tbilisi. Recorded by Street Art Cities without a date, it is part of the dense cluster of independent street art around the Fabrika district.

Nubian Artwork's La Liberté is about being free of burdens, free like the wind that carries the clouds. The mural pairs that idea with an image of flight, where in the air you cannot get your shoes dirty.

Tamoonz painted Fiery Energy on the Tskneti Highway, recalling the unresolved war in Abkhazia and the role of Georgian women who shielded their children from its horrors. The mural frames a woman's mystical, fiery energy as a source of hope in dark times.

Zmicier Zhaunou's Feast treats the Georgian table as an exchange of energy and a symbol of hospitality, happiness and humanity. On Zaza Bendeliani Street, it ranges from quiet coffee to a party, and closes with a toast to freedom.

Goga Katsarava made this mural as a protest against the war in Ukraine. Working in an abstract style, he depicts common iconographic shapes in which good defeats evil, and his team nicknamed the piece after the Georgian national hero Kakutsa Cholokashvili.
Tamoonz painted A Rugby Player Girl for the Niko movement festival in 2021 on Vazha Pshavela Avenue. The sports-themed figure is one of several festival works that celebrate Georgian athletics.

Matthias Mross painted Traffic Lights for the 4GB festival during the second Niko festival in 2019. The mural stands on a rural road outside Tbilisi, part of the programme that carried street art beyond the capital centre.

Kelber's Air was made for the second Niko festival in Tbilisi in 2019. Sharing the building at 30/2 Bakhtrioni Street with In Love, the mural is part of the festival's cluster of works in the neighbourhood.

Matthias Mross painted Urban Cowboy for the third Niko festival in Tbilisi in 2020. On a wall in the Varketili district, the mural adds a wry, playful figure to the eastern edge of the city's street-art map.

Dilk and Ferosone's Nature imagines the spirit of nature balancing against the modern obsession with time and money. On Vasil Barnov Street, the mural suggests that when people find balance with nature, they also find balance within themselves.

Ninuka's 8 March is dedicated to the shared connection that everyone is a child of women. Three stages of a woman's life pass across the wall, supported by a white swan and a lotus, the composition forming the shape of an eight, the sign of infinity.

Dante's Pigs on the Wings is the second of five murals inspired by Pink Floyd's 1977 album Animals. This wall represents the track Pigs on the Wing, part one, part of a series scattered across Tbilisi.

Dziya and Ramas Janotau's Reap What You Sow invokes Mambera, the pagan god who bound wolves' jaws with red thread to spare the honest and loosed them on the dishonest. Inscriptions remind viewers to answer for their actions.

Peter Skensved's David Agmashenebeli was made with the Georgian street art federation in 2023, on Anton Purtseladze Street. The mural brings together collaborators including Vaska Shuradze, Alex and Levan Dadvani, Luka Japaridze and Chxivi.

Nina Khurtsilava dedicated Olechka to her Ukrainian grandmother, a woman who survived the Holodomor and the Second World War. Symbols carry the story: a golden sun for new life, wheat for hope, an acorn for survival, and colours blending Ukraine and Georgia.

Dante and Tsitsqo painted Jump as a basketball-court mural for the Niko Movement festival in 2021. Like Champions, it turns a sports surface into the artwork, so the mural is completed by the players who use it.
Gamez made My Moon (Monkey) for the second Niko festival in Tbilisi in 2019. On Irakli Abashidze Street in Vake, the mural is part of the artist's playful animal imagery across the festival's walls.

Mishiko Sulakauri painted Wind Is Blowing for the third Niko festival in Tbilisi in 2020. The mural in the Varketili district uses movement and breeze as its theme, adding a lighter note to the housing estate.
Lapiz's One Mother argues that we are all children of one mother. A woman's face is assembled from many different faces, dissolving the ideas of them and us and, with them, borders.

Gamez's Fisherman is a tribute to Niko Pirosmani's famous painting of the same name. Painted for the Niko movement in 2018 on Dimitri Uznadze Street, it reworks a Georgian art classic on a public wall.
Dante painted miss you for the third Niko festival in Kutaisi. On Tsereteli Street, the mural is one of several festival works that spread contemporary street art through the city beyond the centre.

Matthias Mross painted Knowledge Is Power for the mural festival at Kutaisi International University. It belongs to the campus cluster of works that place international artists' murals around the university site near Chognari.

Artez painted Girl With Cat for the mural festival at Kutaisi International University. The piece is one of a group of campus walls that gather festival artists at the university site, bringing colour to the student environment.

Dog with Hand is a Street Art Cities entry on Egnate Ninoshvili Street in Tbilisi, recorded without an attributed artist. It sits in the busy Fabrika area, adding to the cluster of independent murals there.

Cocaine is recorded on Kote Afkhazi Street in the old town of Tbilisi, with no artist named by Street Art Cities. The mural adds to the dense layer of street art that coats the lanes of the historic centre.

Williann's Red Riding Hood answers a client's request for something not Georgian but French. The artist chose Charles Perrault's tale and found it just as popular in Georgia, painting the character in Vazisubani in Tbilisi.
Nean's Our Own Roof is recorded on a Tbilisi street marked only as 7a, in the Varketili area. The mural belongs to the city's independent street-art layer, away from the larger festival commissions.

title.en: Pomegranate and oak. Thyme and rose

description.en: Griss Lugard created this amulet mural for the residents of Vake, representing Belarusian and Georgian plants that have historically stood for vitality, eternity and revolution. Pomegranate and oak, thyme and rose express the two nations' shared aspiration for prosperity and independence.

nascaone's Feline Dancer started from a plastic relief at the Fabrika complex and the Georgian epic The Knight in the Panther's Skin. There is a dance school in the building, so the panther became a dancing cat, the artist adding a nod to his Peruvian roots.

Dilk and Ferosone reimagined Flying Painter, a famous character by the Georgian stage designer Petre Otskheli. Produced by the Niko movement in 2018 on Kote Marjanishvili Street, the mural brings theatre design into the street.

Dante and Tsitsqo painted Big Face as a basketball-court mural for the Niko Movement festival in 2021. The court doubles as the artwork, continuing the festival's run of murals painted directly onto sports grounds.

Dilk and Ferosone made Home for the second Niko festival in Tbilisi in 2019. On a wall listed simply as number 50 in the Varketili area, the mural is part of the festival's spread across the city's outskirts.

Lion Fleischmann painted Girl vs Dragon for the third Niko festival in Tbilisi in 2020. The mural in the Varketili district pits a young figure against a dragon, a classic confrontation scaled onto a housing-estate wall.

Dinho Bento's End of War carries the message to look beyond roots, break the weapons and celebrate the end of war. Painted for the Niko movement in 2018 at Elektrowerk in Tbilisi, it is one of the festival's most pacifist works.

Linda and Axel's Peace is recorded on a Tbilisi street marked as 29a, in the Varketili area. The anti-war title recurs across the city's festival murals, giving a housing-estate wall a clear pacifist message.

Irakli Qadeishvili and Zviad Esartia painted Care for the mural festival at Kutaisi International University. It joins the campus cluster of works that line the university site near Chognari, brought together by the festival.
INO painted this wall for Tbilisi Mural Fest 2020, in the north of the city. It belongs to the festival's programme of large international commissions and is recorded by Street Art Cities.
Irakli Kadeishvili made this mural for Tbilisi Mural Fest 2021. Recorded by Street Art Cities at a city-centre address, it is part of the festival's spread of large walls across Tbilisi.
Kera created this mural for Tbilisi Mural Fest 2022 on Ana Politkovskaia Street. It joins the festival's run of large walls across Tbilisi and is documented by Street Art Cities.
Fintan Magee painted this mural for Tbilisi Mural Fest 2022 on Bakhtrioni Street. It belongs to the festival's collection of large figurative walls documented by Street Art Cities.
Luis Gomez made this mural for Tbilisi Mural Fest 2022 on Kote Makashvili Street. Recorded by Street Art Cities, it adds to the festival's cluster of works in central Tbilisi.
Shozy painted this wall for Tbilisi Mural Fest 2024 in Varketili, on Sesilia Takaishvili Street. It is part of the festival's continued programme of commissions across Tbilisi's districts.
Wietse painted this mural at the skater park on Rome Street for Tbilisi Mural Fest 2019. The artwork, recorded by Street Art Cities, marks one of the festival's early walls.
Wedo finished this mural on Lado Asatiani Street in October 2024 for Tbilisi Mural Fest. It is one of the festival's newer walls and is documented by Street Art Cities.

title.en: Tbilisi Mural Fest — Noah Kauertz & Aphe

description.en: Noah Kauertz and Aphe painted this wall on Bakhtrioni Street for Tbilisi Mural Fest. Recorded by Street Art Cities, the work belongs to the festival's growing series of collaborations.
The collective Farm Prod. painted this wall for Tbilisi Mural Fest on Egnate Ninoshvili Street. Founded in Brussels in 2003, the group unites several visual artists around shared creative projects.

title.en: Tbilisi Mural Fest — Luka Japaridze & V45

description.en: Luka Japaridze and V45 made this mural for Tbilisi Mural Fest near Bolo Rise. Recorded by Street Art Cities, it is part of the festival's programme of local and international collaborations.
Giorgi Maskharashvili painted this wall for Tbilisi Mural Fest at 182 Davit Aghmashenebeli Avenue. The mural is documented by Street Art Cities as part of the festival's city-wide programme.

El Bocho made this mural for Tbilisi Mural Fest at 182 Davit Aghmashenebeli Avenue, on the same building as another festival wall. Documented by Street Art Cities, it belongs to the festival's series.
Artez painted this mural for Tbilisi Mural Fest in Varketili III micro-district. Located near a park, the wall is documented by Street Art Cities as part of the festival's spread across the city.

Innerfields painted this wall for the KIU Mural Fest at Kutaisi International University. Recorded by Street Art Cities, it belongs to the festival's cluster of works at the university site near Chognari.
Irakli Kadeishvili painted this wall for Tbilisi Mural Fest 2025 (Kutaisi) on Nikea II Lane. Documented by Street Art Cities, it is one of the festival's recent Kutaisi commissions.
INO painted this mural for Tbilisi Mural Fest 2024 (Kutaisi) on Nikea Street. Recorded by Street Art Cities, it continues the festival's programme in the city's Nikea district.
Cristian Scutaru made this wall for Tbilisi Mural Fest 2024 (Kutaisi). The mural is documented by Street Art Cities and forms part of the festival's growing Kutaisi collection.

title.en: Tbilisi Mural Fest 2020 (Kutaisi, KIU) — Case Maclaim

description.en: Case Maclaim painted this wall for the 2020 KIU Mural Fest at Kutaisi International University. Recorded by Street Art Cities, it is one of the festival's works at the university site near Chognari.

A mural of the Black Sea's white-sided dolphins, painted in grey and black across a concrete fence on Queen Tamara Street in Poti. The artist is not named by the sources; the work is recorded by Madloba and Red Fedora Diary.

A Poti mural depicting the journey of Jason and the Argonauts in search of the golden fleece, signed by S. Khazalia. It stands on the embankment, part of the shoreline group of murals; Madloba dates it to 2023.

A mural dedicated to Niko Nikoladze, showing his portrait with the Poti seaport and its lighthouse, signed by S. Khazalia. It marks the corner of the Rustaveli Embankment and Merab Kostava Street in Poti.

Alexander Isakov's Abstract distils Batumi's architecture, objects and ornaments into his own visual language. The artist gathers the signs each city creates and translates them into abstraction, making a wall that reads as a study of place rather than a single scene.

Roberto Rivadaneira painted this abstract wall for the Niko Movement festival in Batumi in 2021. Set on Vakhtang Gorgasali Street, the piece adds a large non-figurative work to the city's festival run along the coast.

Gamze Yalçın made this abstract mural for the Niko Movement festival in Batumi in 2021, on Zurab Gorgiladze Street. The work belongs to the festival's spread of non-figurative commissions through the resort city.
Skirl (sskirl) painted this abstract wall for the Niko Movement festival in Tbilisi in 2021. On Akaki Tsereteli Avenue, it belongs to the festival's series of non-figurative works across the city.
Kera's Abstract was made for Tbilisi Mural Fest on Bakhtrioni Street. The wall is part of the festival's early programme and adds a non-figurative note to a street that holds several festival murals.

Musya's Amirani (Prometheus) portrays Georgia as the chained mythological hero, surrounded by three crows that stand for the Russian flag. The artist describes it as a commemoration of the ongoing annexation of 20 percent of the country, making the wall openly political.

Skirl (sskirl) painted this abstract basketball-court mural for the Niko Movement festival in Kutaisi in 2021. Painting the court itself turns the playing surface into the artwork, so the mural is completed by the players who use it.

Sali Nikolaishvili made Cosmic Girl for the third Niko festival in Kutaisi in 2020. On Joseb Grishashvili Street, the mural adds a figure to the city's festival collection and is distinct from the Tbilisi Cosmic Girl by Musya.

Innerfields painted Trust for the KIU Mural Fest at Kutaisi International University in 2020. The work is part of the campus cluster of murals that gathers festival artists at the university site near Chognari.

Anunnak's Hunter stands at the corner of Gia Chanturia Street and Shota Rustaveli Avenue in Tbilisi. Recorded by Street Art Cities with title and artist confirmed, it is a separate work from the Feo Flip mural of the same name elsewhere in the city.
